candidateDecisions.label: Mathematical Economics, climate and public policy
Actuarial Science and insurance risk
candidateDecisions.reason: Probability and finance support general risk analysis. The available courses do not form a dedicated actuarial curriculum in insurance loss models, premiums, reserves and life contingencies.

analysis: The closest schedule gives economics and econometrics substantive depth through economic models, regression, causal analysis and public economics, alongside calculus, probability, programming, numerical methods and optimisation. Ethics adds reasoning about decisions, and machine learning contributes predictive methods. Econometrics and Advanced Calculus are directly relevant on their course descriptions. The operations research option develops implementation through databases, software, algorithms, probability, decision modelling and optimisation, with reinforcement learning after the decision course. AI Ethics supports the evaluation of automated decisions. Its business context comes from venture foundations and organisational research. Neural networks supply additional modelling methods. The climate and policy direction adds climate science, environmental spatial analysis, life-cycle assessment and a renewable-energy project to economic and quantitative analysis. Sustainability Essentials II also provides preparation for system design. Linear Systems contributes signals, transformation and dynamic-system methods; it does not stand in for advanced linear algebra. OR Modelling pairs with actual constrained linear programming, Discrete OR with actual dynamic programming and network methods, and Stochastic Models with Markov models, each with different application coverage. Queueing, actuarial mathematics, specialist convexity and dynamic econometrics remain visible separately. Finance and probability can support risk reasoning, while the workbook offers no sustained combination of life contingencies, actuarial loss and reserve models or premiums. The actuarial decision rests on coverage, rather than offering gaps.
